name: banana bread
instructions:
Two variants, rebuilt from scratch (September 2026). VARIANT A is ZAYNAB ISSA's banana cake (Third Culture Cooking) — butter-based, sturdier fluffy cake, takes a GANACHE ON TOP. VARIANT B is NICOLE RUCKER's classic (Fat + Flour) — sour-cream-based, gooey and dense, chocolate chips inside with the nuts, no topping needed.

=== VARIANT A — ZAYNAB ISSA'S BANANA CAKE (BUTTER; GANACHE ON TOP) ===

Makes one 8x8 cake. The butter makes it a STURDIER, FLUFFY cake — the one that supports a glaze.

INGREDIENTS:
- 2-3 large overripe bananas (~1 cup / 215g mashed)
- 1 cup (130g) all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 3/4 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt (if salted butter: reduce to 1/4 tsp)
- 1/3 cup (75g) unsalted butter
- 3/4 cup (150g) sugar
- 2 large eggs
- 1 tsp vanilla extract

PROCEDURE:
1. Preheat to 350°F. Line an 8x8 baking dish with parchment (bottom and sides).
2. Mash the bananas with a fork (~1 cup / 215g).
3. Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl.
4. CREAM the butter and sugar with a mixer until pale and airy, 1-2 min. Eggs one at a time; then vanilla and bananas; then the dry — mix until no dry flour remains.
5. Bake 20-25 min, until a tester comes out mostly clean. Cool ~20 min in the pan, then INVERT onto a platter and peel the parchment — BOTTOM SIDE UP gives a flat surface for glazing.
6. TOP: [[chocolate-ganache]] — or her TAHINI FUDGE (below), which subs natural PEANUT BUTTER for the tahini cleanly.

ZAYNAB'S TAHINI FUDGE (the book's topping): 1/4 cup heavy cream + 1/4 cup water set aside; combine 1/4 cup (45g) semisweet chocolate chips, 1/4 cup (50g) sugar, 1/4 tsp kosher salt in a small heavy pot over medium-low with a few tbsp of the watered cream; whisk until melted, keep adding cream a few tbsp at a time; add 2 tbsp tahini (OR natural peanut butter); whisk until thickened but pourable, 6-10 min total. Pour over the cake, spread to the edges; flaky salt + toasted sesame seeds; vanilla ice cream optional. Both cake and fudge keep 2 days ahead (fudge in the fridge, reheat in 20-sec microwave bursts; cake wrapped at room temp; assemble before serving).

=== VARIANT B — NICOLE RUCKER'S CLASSIC (SOUR CREAM; CHIPS INSIDE) ===

Makes one 9x5 loaf. The sour cream makes it GOOEY AND DENSE — it doesn't really support a frosting or ganache, and that's fine: I put CHOCOLATE CHIPS INSIDE with the nuts instead.

INGREDIENTS:
- 4 medium (472g) very ripe bananas
- 2/3 cup (158ml) neutral oil (grapeseed), + more for the pan
- 1 cup packed (213g) dark-brown sugar
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 2 large eggs
- 1/3 cup (85g) full-fat sour cream
- 1 1/2 cups (187g) all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp ground cinnamon
- 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
- 1 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt
- 1 cup (114g) roughly chopped walnuts or pecans, TOASTED (her optional; I use them)
- CHOCOLATE CHIPS, folded in with the nuts (my addition)
- 3 tbsp (36g) demerara sugar (the crunchy sugar-top crust)

PROCEDURE:
1. Preheat to 350°F. Oil a 9x5 loaf pan and line with parchment.
2. Smash the bananas in a large bowl. Add oil, brown sugar, vanilla, eggs, sour cream; whisk.
3. Whisk the dry (flour, soda, powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt); FOLD into the banana mixture just combined. Fold in the nuts + chocolate chips. Into the pan; sprinkle the surface with demerara sugar.
4. Bake 40-50 min on the center rack, until a skewer comes out clean and the top is set and browned. Cool 30 min in the pan, then wire rack. Keeps sealed at room temp up to a week.
notes:
=== THE POINT — CHOCOLATE + PEANUT BUTTER PAIRING (UNUSUAL FOR A CAKE/LOAF) ===

The best thing about banana bread: its pairing with CHOCOLATE (ganache or chips) and PEANUT BUTTER — unusual for a cake/loaf. Variant A carries it as a ganache/fudge ON TOP (Zaynab's tahini fudge takes the peanut butter substitution natively); variant B carries it as chips INSIDE.

=== THE VARIANT SPLIT — BUTTER vs SOUR CREAM ===

- VARIANT A (Zaynab, BUTTER, creamed): sturdier, fluffy — the cake that supports a glaze. Bottom-side-up inversion for the flat glazing surface.
- VARIANT B (Nicole, SOUR CREAM + oil, whisked): gooey, dense — doesn't really support a frosting or ganache, and that's fine. Chips inside; demerara crunch on top instead. (Her hallmarks: melted/liquid fat, sour cream or yogurt, crunchy baked sugar-top crust.)

=== SOURCES ===

- Variant A: Zaynab Issa, Third Culture Cooking (banana cake with tahini fudge).
- Variant B: Nicole Rucker, Fat + Flour (the classic that opens her banana-bread chapter).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===
